To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
axon-glia interactions are crucial for the long-term integrity of axons.
glial cells support the integrity of myelinated axons and that this process is independent of myelination.
glial cells not only support axonal impulse conduction by myelinating axons but also contribute to axonal maintenance by providing trophic support.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of axon-glio interactions and the function of glial cells in the maintenance of axon integrity.
the molecular basis of the axon-glia interactions in the central and the peripheral nervous system.
the molecular mechanisms that govern the glial support and myelination of axons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
glial support of neuronal function is an important and independent function of glia that is not yet fully understood.
glial support is essential for the long-term functional integrity of axons.
axon-glial interaction is essential to maintain axon function, which is independent of myelination.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
glia are not only the support of axon conduction but also the support of axonal function.
the glial cells that myelinate axon are also responsible for their support and that this support may require glial-specific proteins and intact peroxisome function.
glial cells have a dual function in the nervous system: they support axons, and they myelinate them.
The main takeaway from our work is that
glial cells do much more than simply wrap axons with myelin.
axon-glia interactions are essential for axonal maintenance and that the molecular basis of this interaction is poorly understood.
glia are not simply passive bystanders in axonal support but rather are active players.
